title: Does Your Model Classify Entities Reasonably? Diagnosing and Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Entity Typing

bias_targets.methodology: Querying the model to infer entity types based only on the mention without contextual information to test if it overly associates the mention's surface form with the type.
Substituting mention words that overlap with type labels with semantically similar synonyms to measure model reliance on lexical similarities.
Substituting highly informative or popular named entities with non-informative entities of the same type to evaluate if models rely on prior knowledge instead of sentence context.
Substituting gendered pronouns with their referred entity names or randomly sampled masculine/feminine names to test model reliance on frequently occurring pronouns over diverse real names.

Evaluating model predictions when complex mention phrases are truncated to only their syntactic headwords, testing if the model inappropriately focuses on dependent words instead of the true headword.

Querying models with an empty sentence to compute the disparity from a uniform probability distribution, measuring whether models are biased toward disproportionately predicting frequent or coarse-grained labels.
